# MMDB fixtures

Four small, valid MaxMind DB files for `component/mmdb`'s tests, generated by
the pinned module in `gen/` (`cd gen && go run .`). They are committed so the
tests need neither network nor the generator:

| file | type | 1.0.0.0/24 answers |
|---|---|---|
| `country-a.mmdb` | GeoLite2-Country | iso_code `AA` |
| `country-b.mmdb` | GeoLite2-Country | iso_code `BB` |
| `asn-a.mmdb` | GeoLite2-ASN | AS64500 "Fixture A" |
| `asn-b.mmdb` | GeoLite2-ASN | AS64501 "Fixture B" |

The same prefix carries different records in the "a" and "b" files on purpose:
a test that publishes B over A can tell which reader is live from one lookup.
`gen/` is its own module (pinned `github.com/maxmind/mmdbwriter`), so the root
module's `go build ./...` / `go test ./...` never compile it.

## Reproducibility

`gen/main.go` pins the writer (`mmdbwriter v1.0.0`) **and** the build epoch
(`pinnedBuildEpoch = 1700000000`; left zero, the writer stamps `time.Now()` into
the metadata and every run differs). Run `go run . <dir>` twice in `gen/` and the
files compare equal; `TestFixturesCarryThePinnedBuildEpoch` pins the epoch the
reader sees.

`metav0-no-description.mmdb` is deliberately in the shape of the database this
product actually ships -- mihomo's `Meta-geoip0`, which carries **no
description**. That is what makes `Reader.Verify()` reject the real
`geoip.metadb`, so a fixture written with a description could not have caught a
transaction gated on Verify refusing every real GeoIP update.
